instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Cover the rice, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, start the paste. Roughly chop the 4 shallots and the 3 garlic cloves. Peel the galangal and chop 2 tbsp of it. Cut the 2 green chilies open, scrape out the seeds and chop them.
Finely chop the stems from about 6 sprigs of the cilantro. Pull the stems off 3 of the lime leaves and chop the leaves finely. Crush the 1 tsp peppercorns with the bottom of a heavy pan.
Put everything from the last two steps in a blender or mini chopper with 1/2 tsp shrimp paste and 2 tbsp water. Blend to a smooth paste, scraping down the sides a few times.
Slice the pork into 1/4 inch medallions. Pat them dry and sprinkle the 1/2 tsp salt over them.
Peel and seed the squash and cut half of it into 1/2 inch cubes. That should be about 3 cups. Cut the 5 eggplants into quarters.
Cut the long beans into 1 inch pieces. Slice 3 tbsp of the krachai into thin strips. Pick the leaves off the basil.
Heat 3 tbsp oil in a wok or large pot over medium heat. Add the paste and fry it, stirring often, until it darkens a shade and smells fragrant, 3 to 4 minutes. Stand back a little. It can spit.
Turn the heat up to medium-high. Add the pork and stir fry for about 2 minutes, until it's no longer pink on the outside.
Add the eggplant, the 2 cups broth and 2 tbsp of the fish sauce. Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat down and simmer for 5 minutes.
Tear the last 4 lime leaves and add them with the krachai, 1 tbsp palm sugar and the squash. Simmer for about 10 minutes, until the squash is almost tender when you poke it.

Add the long beans and simmer for 4 minutes, until they're bright green and just tender. The pork is done at 145°F. If you have a thermometer, check a thick slice. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the 3 bird's eye chilies and mix them with the last 1 tbsp fish sauce in a small bowl.
Off the heat, stir in the basil leaves.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the jasmine rice, with the chili fish sauce on the side.
method_notes: No version had 20 or more ratings, Simply Suwanee blocked the page and RecipeTin Eats has no jungle curry, so this leads with the Hairy Bikers' pork version. All three make a coconut free paste of chilies, shallot, garlic, galangal and shrimp paste, fry it in oil, add the meat, then simmer it in stock with Thai eggplant, long beans, makrut lime leaves, krachai, fish sauce and palm sugar, finishing with holy basil. The Hairy Bikers add butternut squash and pea eggplants and leave out lemongrass; Kvalifood and Marion's Kitchen (made with chicken, 4.8 stars on the page with no confirmed count) put lemongrass and dried chilies in the paste. This follows the lead with squash, drops the optional pea eggplants and green peppercorns, and keeps the pot mild with 2 seeded green chilies in the paste and the bird's eye chilies in fish sauce on the side.
